subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 LANDED - THE REFUTATION IS REPAIRED. The row was held at PARTIAL by one operand spelling: when data-name-1 was QUALIFIED the compiler used the value of a DIFFERENT data item, silently, so GR2's 'the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1' was the page size of whatever item of that name happened to be declared first. The mechanism was in the binder, and the row's code-location now names it: BindLinageClause kept only the first word of the operand's dataReference and ResolveFiles resolved that bare word with `ByName.TryGetValue(n) -> list[0]`. Both are gone. The operand keeps its IN/OF qualifiers and resolves through DataBinder.QualifiedCandidates - the ONE 8.4.2.2 candidate-set matcher, shared with the procedure division's ReferenceResolver, which knows the file-name qualifier of 8.4.2.2.2 Format 1 and returns the SET so that the NUMBER of survivors is the answer 8.4.2.2.1 demands. MEASURED, on the probe the refutation named: `LINAGE IS SZ OF GRP-B LINES` over GRP-A.SZ=3 and GRP-B.SZ=9 with `WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING 4 LINES` reported EOP / LINAGE-COUNTER 1 (a 3-line page) before and reports NO-EOP / LINAGE-COUNTER 5 (the correct 9-line page) now, at every edition. The third spelling - an AMBIGUOUS unqualified operand - is now REJECTED (COBOL1639) instead of resolved by declaration order. The row's cost disclosure about the page body's POSITION under a top margin is GR4's obligation and is recorded there; GR2's own sentence is clean.
